assessment.nobel_worthiness: The collateral-based propagation mechanism fundamentally changed macroeconomic analysis of credit crises and policy.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore supplied the core collateral-cycle mechanism, while Gertler was central to its financial-accelerator integration into macroeconomics.
assessment.maturity: The contribution is decades old, extensively developed, and repeatedly tested in crisis-oriented macro-finance research.
uncertainties: The closely related contributions of Simon Gilchrist complicate a three-person attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection supplied a durable framework for understanding trade patterns, productivity, and welfare.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the indispensable originator of the canonical model; Helpman and Redding made major complementary theoretical and empirical contributions.
assessment.maturity: Its implications have been absorbed throughout modern trade research and applied policy analysis.
uncertainties: The breadth of the literature makes the boundary between foundational and subsequent contributors difficult to draw.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework gave quantitative content to a central explanation for large productivity and income gaps.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow produced the especially influential empirical-accounting framework, with Restuccia a leading architect of the broader research programme.
assessment.maturity: The framework has generated a large body of measurement, theory, and policy work over many years.
uncertainties: Interpretation of measured wedges and their causal policy implications remains contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidity models and their monetary-policy implications form a principal organizing framework of contemporary macroeconomics.
assessment.attribution: Calvo pricing, Taylor rules, and Woodford's intertemporal monetary framework are individually identifiable pillars of the synthesis.
assessment.maturity: The ideas are long established in research, central-bank practice, and graduate instruction.
uncertainties: The candidate combines many distinct advances and cannot fully recognize all pivotal contributors within the prize limit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their intertemporal approach reshaped international macroeconomics and clarified persistent exchange-rate and external-adjustment puzzles.
assessment.attribution: Obstfeld and Rogoff jointly supplied a coherent and highly influential framework for the field.
assessment.maturity: The programme has been foundational for several decades and has survived extensive theoretical and empirical scrutiny.
uncertainties: Some key exchange-rate puzzles remain unresolved, limiting a clean claim of explanatory closure.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression transformed empirical analysis by making distributional effects estimable rather than peripheral.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett introduced the foundational method and are the clearest attribution for the central discovery.
assessment.maturity: The method is mature, broadly used across economics, and has stimulated a deep econometric literature.
uncertainties: The longlist formulation also includes later distributional methods whose attribution is less unified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Modern political economics has made institutions, electoral incentives, and state capacity analytically central to fiscal and development outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini established core political-economy models, while Besley made major contributions linking theory to state capacity and evidence.
assessment.maturity: The research programme is mature and influential across political economy, public finance, and development.
uncertainties: The field's broad scope makes it difficult to isolate one sufficiently bounded discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models have materially improved analysis of redistribution, inequality, and the transmission of macroeconomic policy.
assessment.attribution: Kaplan, Moll, and Violante are closely associated with the modern tractable framework and its influential applications.
assessment.maturity: The approach is already central to frontier macroeconomic work and has substantial policy relevance.
uncertainties: The programme is comparatively recent and its empirical validation and ultimate attribution boundaries are still developing.
